- **self**: UI automation of menu bar apps XCUITest and Accessibility API (9/3)

## Structure and components

- [statement] XCUITest and the Accessibility API (AXUIElement) are the same technology underneath; XCUITest is a restricted predefined layer. Raw AX use requires the host binary to be granted in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility before running. (medium confidence) — https://research.macpaw.com/publications/how-to-parse-macos-app-ui · keywords: UI automation of menu bar apps XCUITest and Accessibility API · also: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/794253
- [statement] AX hierarchies can be wrong for NSHostingView-based UI; MacPaw uses a hit-test technique at coordinates to reach hidden layers. (low confidence) — https://research.macpaw.com/publications/how-to-parse-macos-app-ui · keywords: UI automation of menu bar apps XCUITest and Accessibility API

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Apple does not support the Accessibility APIs in sandboxed apps. In a sandboxed menu bar app AXIsProcessTrusted returns false, the prompt never appears, and the app cannot be added in System Settings; with the com.apple.security.accessibility entitlement AX calls can still fail with .cannotComplete. A DTS engineer called this behaviour correct, in both local and TestFlight builds. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/794253 · keywords: UI automation of menu bar apps XCUITest and Accessibility API · also: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/810677

## Facts and statements

- [statement] XCUITest can find a menu bar status item with app.menuBars.statusItems and click it; a launch test can assert existence with app.menuBars.statusItems.firstMatch without checking isHittable. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/tomada1114/hintjump/pull/32 · keywords: UI automation of menu bar apps XCUITest and Accessibility API · also: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/773715
- [statement] Content of a SwiftUI MenuBarExtra(.window) popover is not reliably in the accessibility tree under XCUITest; the safe launch guarantee is that the status item exists. Workaround: a DEBUG-only launch hook that opens the target window deterministically, or an NSStatusItem with an NSMenu and button accessibility label. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/dylblake/NoteSide/pull/11 · keywords: UI automation of menu bar apps XCUITest and Accessibility API · also: https://github.com/tomada1114/macos-app-template/pull/76
- [statement] If Xcode runs fullscreen, the menu bar is hidden and the status item test fails with 'Element StatusItem ... is not hittable'. Leave fullscreen before the run, or post a CGEvent mouse move near the top edge to reveal the menu bar (a reported, self-described ugly workaround). (low confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/773715 · keywords: UI automation of menu bar apps XCUITest and Accessibility API
- [statement] On macOS Sequoia and later, XCTest UI tests prompt for a password to enable UI automation before each run, blocking CI. The accepted forum fix is `automationmodetool enable-automationmode-without-authentication`; disabling SIP and editing TCC did not help. This is a user-to-user answer, not an Apple statement. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/793307 · keywords: UI automation of menu bar apps XCUITest and Accessibility API
- [statement] Sandbox-safe alternatives to AX window inspection (CGWindow list, ScreenCaptureKit) need Screen Recording consent; AppleEvents exceptions are temporary and unsuitable for App Store distribution. A network monitor should not add them for testing. (low confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/794253 · keywords: UI automation of menu bar apps XCUITest and Accessibility API
- [statement] Headless CI use: a shared Xcode scheme lets xcodebuild test run the UI test target without opening Xcode; the runner/helper needs Accessibility consent on first use. (low confidence) — https://github.com/dylblake/NoteSide/pull/11 · keywords: UI automation of menu bar apps XCUITest and Accessibility API
